headline: BARRICK/NEWMONT $1.95B NGM DEAL: ALL DISPUTES SETTLED, NEWMONT CONSENTS TO NORTH AMERICA GOLD IPO — FOURMILE JOINS 100M-OZ NEVADA COMPLEX
source_name: Barrick Mining Corp (TSX: ABX / NYSE: B)
snippet: Barrick and Newmont announced August 10 a landmark resolution of all outstanding Nevada Gold Mines joint venture disputes: Barrick contributes Fourmile, Newmont contributes Mike and Fiberline into NGM, creating a nearly 100-million-ounce Nevada gold complex, with Newmont paying Barrick US$1.95 billion in consideration. In exchange, Newmont has provided formal consent to Barrick's planned minority-stake IPO of a North American gold company — NYSE/TSX primary listing, expected by year-end 2026 — that will include NGM, Pueblo Viejo, and the newly contributed assets. In a simultaneous Q2 results release, Barrick reported revenue of $5.29 billion, net earnings of $1.22 billion ($0.73/share, up 55% year-on-year), and gold production of 796,000 oz, exceeding the 730,000–770,000 oz guidance range. The $1.95B Newmont payment resolves a years-long dispute over the economic treatment of Fourmile — which sits outside the formal NGM JV boundary in the Cortez district — removing the single largest structural barrier to the North American IPO, the most consequential piece of gold corporate news since Barrick's merger with Randgold in 2018.

headline: K92 MINING KNT Q2: REVENUE +113% TO $205M, $310M NET CASH — STAGE 3 PLANT PROCESSES RECORD 225K TONNES IN PNG
snippet: K92 Mining (TSX: KNT) reported August 10 its strongest quarter in company history: Q2 2026 revenue of US$205.2 million (+113% year-on-year), net income of US$84.6 million ($0.34/share, +116%), and a record net cash position of US$310 million with zero debt. The Stage 3 expansion plant processed a record 225,965 tonnes — a 73% increase from Q2 2025 and 59% increase from Q1 2026 — at a head grade of 6.2 g/t gold with 93.8% metallurgical recovery, the 9th consecutive quarter above the DFS recovery target. Production totalled 42,931 oz gold plus copper and silver by-products. K92's Kainantu underground mine in Papua New Guinea is among the world's highest-grade operating gold systems; at current gold prices of approximately $4,300/oz against sub-$1,000/oz cash costs on the high-grade ore, the company is generating free cash flow at multiples of its original feasibility study assumptions — the textbook operating leverage case for what happens when a high-grade underground mine reaches nameplate expansion capacity during a gold bull market.

headline: GALANTAS GALKF INDIANA CHILE: PORPHYRY COPPER-GOLD SIGNAL EMERGES — DRILL EXPANDED 150% TO 12,500m ON DISSEMINATED MOLYBDENITE IN CORE
source_name: Investing News Network / Galantas Gold (TSX-V: GAL / AIM: GAL)
snippet: Galantas Gold (TSX-V: GAL; AIM: GAL) announced August 10 that visual results from 5,060 metres of drilling at its Indiana project near Copiapó, Chile have identified disseminated sulphide mineralisation including molybdenite, hypogene chalcocite, and bornite within an intense alteration envelope — the classic geochemical fingerprint of a porphyry copper-gold-molybdenum system — prompting an expansion of the drill program from 5,000 metres to 12,500 metres, funded from existing cash. Disseminated molybdenite co-occurring with chalcocite and bornite in a porphyry alteration halo is the same mineral suite present at world-class Chilean porphyry systems including Los Pelambres and Escondida. Indiana sits 6 km from Copiapó with existing road infrastructure; the expanded program will test for the disseminated porphyry system at depth, new mineralised structures not previously exposed at surface, and extensions of the known Bondadosa and Flor de Espino veins — potentially a district-scale discovery in one of the world's most copper-productive regions adjacent to major infrastructure.

headline: ZIJIN DROPS C$5.5B ALLIED GOLD BUYOUT: CHINESE OUTBOUND RULES KILL DEAL — $295M STAKE CLOSES TODAY AS KURMUK-SADIOLA GROWTH FUNDED
source_name: StreetWise Reports / Allied Gold Corp (TSX: AAUC)
snippet: Zijin Mining Group and Allied Gold Corp. (TSX: AAUC) allowed the C$5.5 billion ($3.9B) proposed acquisition to expire at its July 29 deadline, citing no reasonable likelihood remaining regulatory conditions would be met — China's tightened outbound investment controls and persistent political risk in Allied's Mali and Ethiopia assets proving an insurmountable barrier. Instead, Zijin subscribed for 12.8 million newly issued Allied shares at C$32.55 per share for a 9.2% strategic stake at US$295 million, a transaction closing on or about August 10, 2026. Allied will deploy proceeds to complete and ramp up the Kurmuk mine in Ethiopia, expand Sadiola in Mali, and fund Côte d'Ivoire operations. The deal structure shifts Zijin from operator-owner to strategic minority partner — analysts at BMO and National Bank view this as a template for future Chinese engagement with Canadian-listed miners: strategic stakes below CFIUS-equivalent review thresholds rather than control transactions. The C$32.55/share Zijin reference price also establishes an arm's-length transaction value for Allied as an independent company.

headline: BCM RESOURCES TK20: 550m+ PORPHYRY-SKARN AT THOMPSON KNOLLS UTAH COPPER-GOLD — TSXV STOCK SURGES 229% ON HISTORIC INTERCEPT
snippet: BCM Resources Corp. (TSXV: B) reported August 6 that diamond drill hole TK20 at its Thompson Knolls copper-gold-silver-molybdenum project in Utah has intersected over 550 metres of strongly mineralised porphyry and intercalated skarn mineralisation — the largest porphyry intercept in the project's history. TK20 was collared 208 metres northeast of discovery hole TK8 (which previously returned 510 feet of skarn) and drilled vertically to assess true thickness and continuity; the 550+ metre porphyry intersection dramatically expands the known dimensions of the system, suggesting a large intrusive centre capable of generating a district-scale copper-gold-molybdenum ore body. BCM Resources stock surged 229% on the TSXV, making it the top-performing Canadian junior mining stock of the week. Thompson Knolls sits in the Basin and Range geological province of southwest Utah — the same broad tectonic setting as high-profile western US copper discoveries — and BCM controls 100% of the property. The porphyry-skarn geometric relationship in TK20 carries the hallmarks of intrusive-related copper-gold porphyry architecture that has attracted major company attention across the Arizona-Utah-Nevada copper corridor.

headline: THOR EXPLORATIONS THX SEGILOLA NIGERIA: 19.4m @ 3.01 g/t GOLD 346m BELOW OPEN PIT — UNDERGROUND SCOPING STUDY COMMISSIONED
source_name: Value The Markets / Thor Explorations (TSXV/AIM: THX)
snippet: Thor Explorations Ltd (TSXV/AIM: THX) reported August 6 that four company-owned diamond drill rigs operating year-round beneath the Segilola Gold Mine open pit in Nigeria continue to intersect high-grade gold at depth in an area that has received relatively little prior drilling. Best intercepts include SNMDD089 (19.4 metres at 3.01 g/t gold from 346m depth), SNMDD166 (5.3 metres at 5.66 g/t from 300m), and SNMDD179 (2.1 metres at 3.02 g/t from 296.9m and 3.3 metres at 5.99 g/t from 307.7m). Thor has commissioned a mining consultancy to review underground potential and possible open pit extension, targeting an updated resource estimate by year-end 2026. The strategic advantage of this setup: Segilola is a permitted, producing gold mine with existing processing infrastructure, meaning any underground reserve definition can advance directly to mine planning rather than requiring a new permitting process — dramatically reducing development capital risk compared to a greenfield underground discovery.

headline: TRUMP DROPS $2B CRITICAL MINERALS PACKAGE: $1.4B SILICON ANODES, $400M SCANDIUM, $150M RARE-EARTH-FREE MAGNETS — $180M MINING SCHOOLS
snippet: President Trump announced August 7 a coordinated $2+ billion critical minerals and mining investment package: the largest commitment is $1.4 billion to Sila Nanotechnologies for silicon-carbon battery anode production and a US lithium-ion battery cell plant; $400 million to Sunrise Energy Metals for a US scandium supply chain; $150 million to Niron Magnetics for rare-earth-free iron nitride (Fe16N2) permanent magnets; and over $85 million to Standard Bauxite for refractory-grade bauxite security. A parallel $180 million workforce investment funds innovation hubs at the Colorado School of Mines, South Dakota School of Mines, and Johns Hopkins University. The Niron Magnetics commitment is the strategically distinctive item: iron nitride magnets contain no neodymium, dysprosium, or other rare earth elements — if scaled commercially they would reduce US defense dependence on Chinese rare earth magnet supply chains entirely. For junior rare earth and critical minerals developers, the package confirms sustained US government procurement and financing signals beyond existing DOD and Ex-Im Bank programmes.

headline: GOLD $4,328 SILVER $64 HOLD LAST WEEK'S BREAKOUT LEVELS — CPI WEDNESDAY AND PPI THURSDAY COULD TEST OR EXTEND THE BULL MOVE
snippet: Gold held at $4,328 and silver above $64 entering the week of August 10 — the first full trading week after the payrolls-driven breakout that sent GDX +21% and GDXJ +22% in five sessions. The week's critical event risk is US CPI for July (Wednesday, August 12) and PPI (Thursday), with consensus expecting headline CPI at +0.2% month-on-month and core at +0.3%. A hot print could push Treasury yields and the dollar higher, testing whether gold holds above $4,300 — the technical level bull market analysts identified as the key weekly close threshold for the next leg. A soft CPI print at or below consensus would validate the July payrolls miss (-23,000 vs +180,000 consensus) and accelerate the Fed rate-cut timeline, potentially driving gold toward the $4,500–$4,645 next resistance zone. Complication: WTI crude surged 23.5% over the prior month, raising the risk of energy-driven CPI upside that creates a stagflationary scenario — historically supportive for gold even as it complicates the rate-cut calculus.
